text: I think sometimes that if I were only well enough to write a little it would relieve the press of ideas and rest me. But I find I get pretty tired when I try. It is so discouraging not to have any advice and companionship about my work.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: It is so discouraging not to have any advice and companionship about my work. When I get really well John says we will ask Cousin Henry and Julia down for a long visit; but he says he would as soon put fire-works in my pillow-case as to let me have those stimulating people about now.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I wish I could get well faster. But I must not think about that. This paper looks to me as if it knew what a vicious influence it had! There is a recurrent spot where the pattern lolls like a broken neck and two bulbous eyes stare at you upside-down.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I never saw so much expression in an inanimate thing before, and we all know how much expression they have! I used to lie awake as a child and get more entertainment and terror out of blank walls and plain furniture than most children could find in a toy-store.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I remember what a kindly wink the knobs of our big old bureau used to have, and there was one chair that always seemed like a strong friend. I used to feel that if any of the other things looked too fierce I could always hop into that chair and be safe.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I used to feel that if any of the other things looked too fierce I could always hop into that chair and be safe. The furniture in this room is no worse than inharmonious, however, for we had to bring it all from downstairs.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: The furniture in this room is no worse than inharmonious, however, for we had to bring it all from downstairs. I suppose when this was used as a playroom they had to take the nursery things out, and no wonder!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Then the floor is scratched and gouged and splintered, the plaster itself is dug out here and there, and this great heavy bed, which is all we found in the room, looks as if it had been through the wars.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: But I don’t mind it a bit—only the paper. There comes John’s sister. Such a dear girl as she is, and so careful of me! I must not let her find me writing. She is a perfect, and enthusiastic housekeeper, and hopes for no better profession.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: She is a perfect, and enthusiastic housekeeper, and hopes for no better profession. I verily believe she thinks it is the writing which made me sick! But I can write when she is out, and see her a long way off from these windows.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: But I can write when she is out, and see her a long way off from these windows. There is one that commands the road, a lovely, shaded, winding road, and one that just looks off over the country.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: But in the places where it isn’t faded, and where the sun is just so, I can see a strange, provoking, formless sort of figure, that seems to sulk about behind that silly and conspicuous front design.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: There’s sister on the stairs! Well, the Fourth of July is over! The people are gone and I am tired out. John thought it might do me good to see a little company, so we just had mother and Nellie and the children down for a week.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Of course I didn’t do a thing. Jennie sees to everything now. But it tired me all the same. John says if I don’t pick up faster he shall send me to Weir Mitchell in the fall.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: John says if I don’t pick up faster he shall send me to Weir Mitchell in the fall. But I don’t want to go there at all. I had a friend who was in his hands once, and she says he is just like John and my brother, only more so!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I cry at nothing, and cry most of the time. Of course I don’t when John is here, or anybody else, but when I am alone. And I am alone a good deal just now.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: And I am alone a good deal just now. John is kept in town very often by serious cases, and Jennie is good and lets me alone when I want her to. So I walk a little in the garden or down that lovely lane, sit on the porch under the roses, and lie down up here a good deal.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: So I walk a little in the garden or down that lovely lane, sit on the porch under the roses, and lie down up here a good deal. I’m getting really fond of the room in spite of the wallpaper.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I’m getting really fond of the room in spite of the wallpaper. Perhaps because of the wallpaper. It dwells in my mind so! I lie here on this great immovable bed—it is nailed down, I believe—and follow that pattern about by the hour.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I know a little of the principle of design, and I know this thing was not arranged on any laws of radiation, or alternation, or repetition, or symmetry, or anything else that I ever heard of.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: The whole thing goes horizontally, too, at least it seems so, and I exhaust myself in trying to distinguish the order of its going in that direction. They have used a horizontal breadth for a frieze, and that adds wonderfully to the confusion.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: There is one end of the room where it is almost intact, and there, when the cross-lights fade and the low sun shines directly upon it, I can almost fancy radiation after all,—the interminable grotesques seem to form around a common centre and rush off in headlong plunges of equal distraction.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: It makes me tired to follow it. I will take a nap, I guess. I don’t know why I should write this. I don’t want to. I don’t feel able. And I know John would think it absurd.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: And I know John would think it absurd. But I must say what I feel and think in some way—it is such a relief! But the effort is getting to be greater than the relief.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: But the effort is getting to be greater than the relief. Half the time now I am awfully lazy, and lie down ever so much. John says I mustn’t lose my strength, and has me take cod-liver oil and lots of tonics and things, to say nothing of ale and wine and rare meat.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: John says I mustn’t lose my strength, and has me take cod-liver oil and lots of tonics and things, to say nothing of ale and wine and rare meat. Dear John! He loves me very dearly, and hates to have me sick.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: But he said I wasn’t able to go, nor able to stand it after I got there; and I did not make out a very good case for myself, for I was crying before I had finished.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: It is getting to be a great effort for me to think straight. Just this nervous weakness, I suppose. And dear John gathered me up in his arms, and just carried me upstairs and laid me on the bed, and sat by me and read to me till it tired my head.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: And dear John gathered me up in his arms, and just carried me upstairs and laid me on the bed, and sat by me and read to me till it tired my head. He said I was his darling and his comfort and all he had, and that I must take care of myself for his sake, and keep well.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: He said I was his darling and his comfort and all he had, and that I must take care of myself for his sake, and keep well. He says no one but myself can help me out of it, that I must use my will and self-control and not let any silly fancies run away with me.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: He says no one but myself can help me out of it, that I must use my will and self-control and not let any silly fancies run away with me. There’s one comfort, the baby is well and happy, and does not have to occupy this nursery with the horrid wallpaper.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: There’s one comfort, the baby is well and happy, and does not have to occupy this nursery with the horrid wallpaper. If we had not used it that blessed child would have! What a fortunate escape!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I never thought of it before, but it is lucky that John kept me here after all. I can stand it so much easier than a baby, you see. Of course I never mention it to them any more,—I am too wise,—but I keep watch of it all the same.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Of course I never mention it to them any more,—I am too wise,—but I keep watch of it all the same. There are things in that paper that nobody knows but me, or ever will.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: There are things in that paper that nobody knows but me, or ever will. Behind that outside pattern the dim shapes get clearer every day. It is always the same shape, only very numerous. And it is like a woman stooping down and creeping about behind that pattern.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: And it is like a woman stooping down and creeping about behind that pattern. I don’t like it a bit. I wonder—I begin to think—I wish John would take me away from here!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: It is so hard to talk with John about my case, because he is so wise, and because he loves me so. But I tried it last night. It was moonlight. The moon shines in all around, just as the sun does.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I hate to see it sometimes, it creeps so slowly, and always comes in by one window or another. John was asleep and I hated to waken him, so I kept still and watched the moonlight on that undulating wallpaper till I felt creepy.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: John was asleep and I hated to waken him, so I kept still and watched the moonlight on that undulating wallpaper till I felt creepy. The faint figure behind seemed to shake the pattern, just as if she wanted to get out.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: The faint figure behind seemed to shake the pattern, just as if she wanted to get out. I got up softly and went to feel and see if the paper did move, and when I came back John was awake.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I thought it was a good time to talk, so I told him that I really was not gaining here, and that I wished he would take me away. “Why darling!” said he, “our lease will be up in three weeks, and I can’t see how to leave before.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: “The repairs are not done at home, and I cannot possibly leave town just now. Of course if you were in any danger I could and would, but you really are better, dear, whether you can see it or not.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: “I don’t weigh a bit more,” said I, “nor as much; and my appetite may be better in the evening, when you are here, but it is worse in the morning when you are away.”
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: “Bless her little heart!” said he with a big hug; “she shall be as sick as she pleases! But now let’s improve the shining hours by going to sleep, and talk about it in the morning!”
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: “And you won’t go away?” I asked gloomily. “Why, how can I, dear? It is only three weeks more and then we will take a nice little trip of a few days while Jennie is getting the house ready.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: “My darling,” said he, “I beg of you, for my sake and for our child’s sake, as well as for your own, that you will never for one instant let that idea enter your mind!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: So of course I said no more on that score, and we went to sleep before long. He thought I was asleep first, but I wasn’t,—I lay there for hours trying to decide whether that front pattern and the back pattern really did move together or separately.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: On a pattern like this, by daylight, there is a lack of sequence, a defiance of law, that is a constant irritant to a normal mind. The color is hideous enough, and unreliable enough, and infuriating enough, but the pattern is torturing.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: The color is hideous enough, and unreliable enough, and infuriating enough, but the pattern is torturing. You think you have mastered it, but just as you get well under way in following, it turns a back somersault and there you are.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: That is, sometimes! There is one marked peculiarity about this paper, a thing nobody seems to notice but myself, and that is that it changes as the light changes. When the sun shoots in through the east window—I always watch for that first long, straight ray—it changes so quickly that I never can quite believe it.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: When the sun shoots in through the east window—I always watch for that first long, straight ray—it changes so quickly that I never can quite believe it. That is why I watch it always.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: That is why I watch it always. By moonlight—the moon shines in all night when there is a moon—I wouldn’t know it was the same paper. At night in any kind of light, in twilight, candlelight, lamplight, and worst of all by moonlight, it becomes bars!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: At night in any kind of light, in twilight, candlelight, lamplight, and worst of all by moonlight, it becomes bars! The outside pattern I mean, and the woman behind it is as plain as can be.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I didn’t realize for a long time what the thing was that showed behind,—that dim sub-pattern,—but now I am quite sure it is a woman. By daylight she is subdued, quiet. I fancy it is the pattern that keeps her so still.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I lie down ever so much now. John says it is good for me, and to sleep all I can. Indeed, he started the habit by making me lie down for an hour after each meal.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Indeed, he started the habit by making me lie down for an hour after each meal. It is a very bad habit, I am convinced, for, you see, I don’t sleep. And that cultivates deceit, for I don’t tell them I’m awake,—oh, no!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: And that cultivates deceit, for I don’t tell them I’m awake,—oh, no! The fact is, I am getting a little afraid of John. He seems very queer sometimes, and even Jennie has an inexplicable look.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: He seems very queer sometimes, and even Jennie has an inexplicable look. It strikes me occasionally, just as a scientific hypothesis, that perhaps it is the paper! I have watched John when he did not know I was looking, and come into the room suddenly on the most innocent excuses, and I’ve caught him several times looking at the paper!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I have watched John when he did not know I was looking, and come into the room suddenly on the most innocent excuses, and I’ve caught him several times looking at the paper! And Jennie too.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: She didn’t know I was in the room, and when I asked her in a quiet, a very quiet voice, with the most restrained manner possible, what she was doing with the paper she turned around as if she had been caught stealing, and looked quite angry—asked me why I should frighten her so!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Then she said that the paper stained everything it touched, that she had found yellow smooches on all my clothes and John’s, and she wished we would be more careful! Did not that sound innocent?
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Did not that sound innocent? But I know she was studying that pattern, and I am determined that nobody shall find it out but myself! Life is very much more exciting now than it used to be.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Life is very much more exciting now than it used to be. You see I have something more to expect, to look forward to, to watch. I really do eat better, and am more quiet than I was.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: John is so pleased to see me improve! He laughed a little the other day, and said I seemed to be flourishing in spite of my wallpaper. I turned it off with a laugh. I had no intention of telling him it was because of the wallpaper—he would make fun of me.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I don’t want to leave now until I have found it out. There is a week more, and I think that will be enough. I’m feeling ever so much better! I don’t sleep much at night, for it is so interesting to watch developments; but I sleep a good deal in the daytime.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: In the daytime it is tiresome and perplexing. There are always new shoots on the fungus, and new shades of yellow all over it. I cannot keep count of them, though I have tried conscientiously.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: It is the strangest yellow, that wallpaper! It makes me think of all the yellow things I ever saw—not beautiful ones like buttercups, but old foul, bad yellow things. But there is something else about that paper—the smell!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: But there is something else about that paper—the smell! I noticed it the moment we came into the room, but with so much air and sun it was not bad. Now we have had a week of fog and rain, and whether the windows are open or not, the smell is here.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: It creeps all over the house. I find it hovering in the dining-room, skulking in the parlor, hiding in the hall, lying in wait for me on the stairs. It gets into my hair.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: It gets into my hair. Even when I go to ride, if I turn my head suddenly and surprise it—there is that smell! Such a peculiar odor, too! I have spent hours in trying to analyze it, to find what it smelled like.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: It is not bad—at first, and very gentle, but quite the subtlest, most enduring odor I ever met. In this damp weather it is awful. I wake up in the night and find it hanging over me.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: It used to disturb me at first. I thought seriously of burning the house—to reach the smell. But now I am used to it. The only thing I can think of that it is like is the color of the paper!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I wonder how it was done and who did it, and what they did it for. Round and round and round—round and round and round—it makes me dizzy! I really have discovered something at last.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I really have discovered something at last. Through watching so much at night, when it changes so, I have finally found out. The front pattern does move—and no wonder! The woman behind shakes it!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Sometimes I think there are a great many women behind, and sometimes only one, and she crawls around fast, and her crawling shakes it all over. Then in the very bright spots she keeps still, and in the very shady spots she just takes hold of the bars and shakes them hard.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Then in the very bright spots she keeps still, and in the very shady spots she just takes hold of the bars and shakes them hard. And she is all the time trying to climb through.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: They get through, and then the pattern strangles them off and turns them upside-down, and makes their eyes white! If those heads were covered or taken off it would not be half so bad.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: If those heads were covered or taken off it would not be half so bad. I think that woman gets out in the daytime! And I’ll tell you why—privately—I’ve seen her! I can see her out of every one of my windows!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I can see her out of every one of my windows! It is the same woman, I know, for she is always creeping, and most women do not creep by daylight. I see her on that long shaded lane, creeping up and down.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I see her on that long shaded lane, creeping up and down. I see her in those dark grape arbors, creeping all around the garden. I see her on that long road under the trees, creeping along, and when a carriage comes she hides under the blackberry vines.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I see her on that long road under the trees, creeping along, and when a carriage comes she hides under the blackberry vines. I don’t blame her a bit. It must be very humiliating to be caught creeping by daylight!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I always lock the door when I creep by daylight. I can’t do it at night, for I know John would suspect something at once. And John is so queer now, that I don’t want to irritate him.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: And John is so queer now, that I don’t want to irritate him. I wish he would take another room! Besides, I don’t want anybody to get that woman out at night but myself. I often wonder if I could see her out of all the windows at once.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I often wonder if I could see her out of all the windows at once. But, turn as fast as I can, I can only see out of one at one time. And though I always see her she may be able to creep faster than I can turn!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: And though I always see her she may be able to creep faster than I can turn! I have watched her sometimes away off in the open country, creeping as fast as a cloud shadow in a high wind.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I have watched her sometimes away off in the open country, creeping as fast as a cloud shadow in a high wind. If only that top pattern could be gotten off from the under one!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: If only that top pattern could be gotten off from the under one! I mean to try it, little by little. I have found out another funny thing, but I shan’t tell it this time!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I have found out another funny thing, but I shan’t tell it this time! It does not do to trust people too much. There are only two more days to get this paper off, and I believe John is beginning to notice.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: There are only two more days to get this paper off, and I believe John is beginning to notice. I don’t like the look in his eyes. And I heard him ask Jennie a lot of professional questions about me.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: And I heard him ask Jennie a lot of professional questions about me. She had a very good report to give. She said I slept a good deal in the daytime. John knows I don’t sleep very well at night, for all I’m so quiet!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: John knows I don’t sleep very well at night, for all I’m so quiet! He asked me all sorts of questions, too, and pretended to be very loving and kind. As if I couldn’t see through him!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: As if I couldn’t see through him! Still, I don’t wonder he acts so, sleeping under this paper for three months. It only interests me, but I feel sure John and Jennie are secretly affected by it.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: It only interests me, but I feel sure John and Jennie are secretly affected by it. Hurrah! This is the last day, but it is enough. John is to stay in town over night, and won’t be out until this evening.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Jennie wanted to sleep with me—the sly thing! but I told her I should undoubtedly rest better for a night all alone. That was clever, for really I wasn’t alone a bit! As soon as it was moonlight, and that poor thing began to crawl and shake the pattern, I got up and ran to help her.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I pulled and she shook, I shook and she pulled, and before morning we had peeled off yards of that paper. A strip about as high as my head and half around the room. And then when the sun came and that awful pattern began to laugh at me I declared I would finish it to-day!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: And then when the sun came and that awful pattern began to laugh at me I declared I would finish it to-day! We go away to-morrow, and they are moving all my furniture down again to leave things as they were before.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: We go away to-morrow, and they are moving all my furniture down again to leave things as they were before. Jennie looked at the wall in amazement, but I told her merrily that I did it out of pure spite at the vicious thing.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Jennie looked at the wall in amazement, but I told her merrily that I did it out of pure spite at the vicious thing. She laughed and said she wouldn’t mind doing it herself, but I must not get tired.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: She laughed and said she wouldn’t mind doing it herself, but I must not get tired. How she betrayed herself that time! But I am here, and no person touches this paper but me—not alive!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: She tried to get me out of the room—it was too patent! But I said it was so quiet and empty and clean now that I believed I would lie down again and sleep all I could; and not to wake me even for dinner—I would call when I woke.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: So now she is gone, and the servants are gone, and the things are gone, and there is nothing left but that great bedstead nailed down, with the canvas mattress we found on it. We shall sleep downstairs to-night, and take the boat home to-morrow.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: But I must get to work. I have locked the door and thrown the key down into the front path. I don’t want to go out, and I don’t want to have anybody come in, till John comes.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I don’t want to go out, and I don’t want to have anybody come in, till John comes. I want to astonish him. I’ve got a rope up here that even Jennie did not find.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I’ve got a rope up here that even Jennie did not find. If that woman does get out, and tries to get away, I can tie her! But I forgot I could not reach far without anything to stand on!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: But I forgot I could not reach far without anything to stand on! This bed will not move! I tried to lift and push it until I was lame, and then I got so angry I bit off a little piece at one corner—but it hurt my teeth.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I tried to lift and push it until I was lame, and then I got so angry I bit off a little piece at one corner—but it hurt my teeth. Then I peeled off all the paper I could reach standing on the floor.
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: Then I peeled off all the paper I could reach standing on the floor. It sticks horribly and the pattern just enjoys it! All those strangled heads and bulbous eyes and waddling fungus growths just shriek with derision!
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
title: The Yellow Wallpaper

text: I am getting angry enough to do something desperate. To jump out of the window would be admirable exercise, but the bars are too strong even to try. Besides I wouldn’t do it. Of course not.

text: We visited the Thousand and One Columns. I do not know what it was originally intended for, but they said it was built for a reservoir. It is situated in the centre of Constantinople. You go down a flight of stone steps in the middle of a barren place, and there you are.
author: Mark Twain

text: We went to the great Bazaar in Stamboul, of course, and I shall not describe it further than to say it is a monstrous hive of little shops —thousands, I should say—all under one roof, and cut up into innumerable little blocks by narrow streets which are arched overhead.
author: Mark Twain

text: I find them every where, but not in strong force. The most I have found together has been about ten or twenty. And night or day a fair proportion of them were sound asleep. Those that were not asleep always looked as if they wanted to be.

text: They sleep in the streets these days. They are my compass—my guide. When I see the dogs sleep placidly on, while men, sheep, geese, and all moving things turn out and go around them, I know I am not in the great street where the hotel is, and must go further.

text: It was curious to see newsboys selling papers in so dreamy a land as that. And, to say truly, it is comparatively a new thing here. The selling of newspapers had its birth in Constantinople about a year ago, and was a child of the Prussian and Austrian war.

text: There is one paper published here in the English language—The Levant Herald—and there are generally a number of Greek and a few French papers rising and falling, struggling up and falling again. Newspapers are not popular with the Sultan's Government.

text: The newspaper business has its inconveniences in Constantinople. Two Greek papers and one French one were suppressed here within a few days of each other. No victories of the Cretans are allowed to be printed.

text: There is only one English newspaper in Naples. It has seventy subscribers. The publisher is getting rich very deliberately—very deliberately indeed. I never shall want another Turkish lunch. title: The Innocents Abroad

text: The Grand Duke is the third brother of the Emperor, is about thirty-seven years old, perhaps, and is the princeliest figure in Russia. He is even taller than the Czar, as straight as an Indian, and bears himself like one of those gorgeous knights we read about in romances of the Crusades.
author: Mark Twain
title: The Innocents Abroad

title: The Innocents Abroad

author: Mark Twain

text: When it was time to go, we bade our distinguished hosts good-bye, and they retired happy and contented to their apartments to count their spoons. title: The Innocents Abroad
